note: No class (000): counties leave it on lots they have not classified
DOR class 1x0: residential land, vacant (plain, unzoned farm land, misc, lakefront, potential development)

DOR class 1x1: residential land, improved (also in a commercial or industrial zone, rural homesite, EFU in a water district, lakefront, potential development). Can't tell detached from attached houses or small plexes on one lot: see the adapter's limitations
DOR residential condominium (102, 122 commercial zone, 192 potential development, 092 misc potential development)
DOR class 4x1: tract land, improved (an acreage homesite; Metro's LANDUSE groups it as RUR). Counted as a house like the ACS one-unit-detached fallback counts rural homes
DOR class 4: tract land, vacant, condominium or manufactured structure
DOR manufactured structure park (707) and manufactured-structure classes (677, 779)
DOR class 7x1: multiple housing, improved (any zone). The class does not record the unit count; assessors use it for apartment properties
DOR class 7: multiple-housing land, vacant, condominium or other (not a single-family lot)
DOR class 2: commercial land (vacant or improved) and misc commercial-zone codes
DOR class 3: industrial land and misc industrial-zone codes
DOR class 9: exempt (student housing, church, school, cemetery, city, county, state, federal, fraternal, port)

Remaining DOR codes: recreation (8xx), misc (0xx, incl. 081 recreation summer-home sites) and residential codes that are neither vacant land nor an improved lot (106 waterfront, 109 exempt, 128, 150, 172)
